father_note: Eron, the village will always look peaceful until it isn't — Bram smiled at me for two years before he moved against me with nothing but his own hunger driving him, and you should never forget a man who showed you that. Sela and her people — Kael, Esa, Vela, Taric — they stood without being asked, and that is the rarest thing this world produces; hold onto them like they are blood, because in the ways that matter they are. Watch Dav's family: they plan quietly and eat well, and quiet planning in a hungry place always comes at someone else's cost. I am not a hard man and I don't ask you to be one, but be harder to move than you look — that alone will keep you alive when words run out.

Father. The pile came up empty this year and you're sitting at one food — that worries me. I have two; take one.

That means more to me than you know, Eron — but keep it. You're young and you need your strength, and a father who drains his son is no kind of father.
Eron gathers Roan to talk.

You already gave me enough by being here — but tell me, are you watching Bram? Seven food, pile empty, and he's never been the kind to hold that much without thinking about how to turn it into something.
Eron gathers Roan to talk.

Watching him every day — seven food when no one else cleared two is either luck or planning, and Bram doesn't rely on luck. If he comes for anyone this year, I think it's you or Kael he moves on first; you're both worth targeting and neither of you has the numbers he'd fear.

Pile went fast and Vela scooped twice — I noticed that. You're at four food, I'm at two; between us we can stay on our feet, but keep your eyes on Mako too, not just Bram, because a man that strong sitting on seven doesn't need much excuse.

Mako worries me more than Bram does, if I'm honest — Bram's made his move and the whole village shut him down, but Mako's never tipped his hand and he's sitting on seven with the arms to back it up. Stay close to Sela and keep Eron visible; a man thinks twice before moving on a family. If Mako starts gifting food or talking to Bram private, you come to me that same hour.

You're right that Mako's the darker unknown — Bram we can read, but Mako's silence is its own kind of warning. I'll stay near Sela and watch who Mako spends words on; if he's building something, he'll need an ally before he acts. Two food won't last me long, so if this year turns lean I may need to lean on you — I'm not ashamed to say it.

mother_note:
Eron, your blood runs from me and from Roan, who stood beside me when the village was still learning what it was — remember that he answered the call without being asked when Bram moved against us, and a man who does that once will likely do it again.

Trust Kael and Esa before almost anyone else; they've said hard things honestly when lying would have cost them less, and that's the rarest thing I've found here. Vela is old and quiet and worth twice what she lets on — don't mistake her small footprint for weakness.

Watch Dell and Dav: they love each other and they move fast, and a family that feeds itself first and asks later is not your enemy until it is — by which point it's too late to start counting.

Bram wronged no one in our blood yet, but he tested this village's patience and found it had teeth; he will try again when he thinks the numbers have shifted, so keep your own count and don't let him catch you standing alone.
